post-tgr-finite-newton-gravity-preparati.physical_scope: Finite N≥2, bounded positive-volume confining box, equal classical masses, fixed positive softening length and inverse-energy parameter; effective Newtonian weak-field/slow-motion model only, with no thermalization or dynamical stability claim.

post-tgr-finite-newton-gravity-preparati:
## Postulate

Work in SI units. Adopt positive Newton constant $G$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, common particle mass $m$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, positions $q_i$ in $\mathrm m$, momenta $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy $H$ in joules, Boltzmann constant $k_B$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. Fix an action reference $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$; it is a phase-counting convention, not an assertion that $h_*$ equals Planck's constant. These conventions follow [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]].

For an integer $N\ge2$, take a bounded measurable confining region $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $0<|B|<\infty$ and adopt the ordered phase space $\Gamma_N=B^N\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and identical-particle reference measure $d\nu_N=d^{3N}q\,d^{3N}p/(N!h_*^{3N})$ of [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]]. Fix a softening length $a>0$ in metres and adopt the Hamiltonian
$$H_{N,a}(q,p)=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{|p_i|^2}{2m}-\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac{Gm^2}{\sqrt{|q_i-q_j|^2+a^2}},$$
which is the model defined in [[def-tgr-softened-gravity-finite-phase]]. The preparation assigns canonical weight $e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}$ relative to $\nu_N$; its normalization is established separately in [[pthm-tgr-regulated-gravity-canonical-equilibrium]]. Reflecting or confining walls specify the finite position region, but no wall dynamics is used in the equilibrium calculation.

Within this formulation, $N,m,G,a,B,h_*$ and $\beta$ are fixed model/preparation inputs. The displayed $H_{N,a}$ is the defined effective Hamiltonian; $Z_N$, the normalized density, mean energy, entropy and response are derived mathematical quantities. Their definition does not make them universal properties of gravitating matter.

This is an adopted effective Newtonian statistical model in a stated weak-field, slow-motion regime. The unbounded momentum domain is part of the canonical mathematical preparation and does not give a uniform speed bound on every point in its support. The postulate asserts neither dynamical equilibration, an observed gravitating gas, nor stability of a self-consistently gravitating relativistic solution.

pthm-tgr-regulated-gravity-canonical-equ.physical_scope: Conditional on the finite equal-mass softened Newtonian model with bounded positive-volume box and fixed a>0; proves normalization, the stated Gibbs variational optimum, and nonnegative fixed-Hamiltonian canonical response, not thermalization or stability of a changing/self-consistent background.

post-tgr-unregulated-point-attempt.physical_scope: Two labelled positive Newtonian point masses in a bounded box with interior and no short-distance cutoff; canonical weight is attempted without assuming a finite normalization. Collision configurations lie outside any asserted controlled weak-field model.

post-tgr-unregulated-point-attempt:
## Postulate

In SI units, take two labelled masses $m_1,m_2>0$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, positions $q_1,q_2$ in a bounded box $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ with nonempty interior, momenta $p_1,p_2$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $G>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. Fix $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$ as the phase-action reference and $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, with the unit conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]]. The labelled-pair phase space is $\Gamma_{12}=B^2\times\mathbb R^6$ with reference measure
$$d\nu_{12}=h_*^{-6}\,d^3q_1\,d^3q_2\,d^3p_1\,d^3p_2.$$
On the off-diagonal domain $q_1\ne q_2$, adopt the unregulated point Hamiltonian
$$H^{\rm pt}_{12}(q,p)=\frac{|p_1|^2}{2m_1}+\frac{|p_2|^2}{2m_2}-\frac{Gm_1m_2}{|q_1-q_2|}.$$
Attempt canonical sampling with weight $e^{-\beta H^{\rm pt}_{12}}$, but do not assume its integral is finite or that the normalized probability law exists. If $m_1=m_2$, the identical-particle reference measure of [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]] is $d\nu_{12}/2$; this constant convention does not alter whether the integral converges.

The masses, $G$, box, action reference and $\beta$ are fixed inputs of this attempted model; $H^{\rm pt}_{12}$ is defined by the formula. A finite partition function or probability law is not a primitive input and is not postulated.

This is a distinct unregulated model, not the softened preparation with $a$ set to zero after normalization. Arbitrarily small separations are not asserted to remain in a controlled Newtonian weak-field regime. The attempted weight is a model specification, not a reported physical preparation or an assertion of successful thermalization.

post-tgr-kepler-canonical-preparation.physical_scope: Effective Newtonian relative two-body Hamiltonian on the fixed hard radial shell r0≤|q|≤R with canonical β>0 preparation; the center-of-mass mode is absent and the unbounded canonical momentum tail has no uniform slow-speed guarantee.

post-tgr-kepler-canonical-preparation:
## Postulate

Use positive masses $m_1,m_2$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, $A=Gm_1m_2>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$, relative position $q\in\mathbb R^3$ in metres, relative momentum $p\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and action reference $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Fix $r_0>0$ and $R>16r_0$. Adopt the relative phase region and Hamiltonian of [[def-tgr-regulated-kepler-shell-law]]:
$$\Gamma_{\rm rel}=\{(q,p):r_0\le|q|\le R,\ p\in\mathbb R^3\},\qquad d\nu_{\rm rel}=h_*^{-3}d^3q\,d^3p,\qquad h(q,p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2\mu}-\frac A{|q|}.$$
There are no center-of-mass variables and no identical-particle factor in this relative phase convention. Adopt a canonical preparation at inverse energy $\beta>0$ with $T_K=(k_B\beta)^{-1}$ and density $p_\beta(q,p)=Z_{\rm rel}(\beta)^{-1}e^{-\beta h(q,p)}$ relative to $d\nu_{\rm rel}$ on all of $\Gamma_{\rm rel}$. Its finite positive normalizer and normalized density follow from [[lem-tgr-relative-shell-canonical-response]]. Since $h$ is finite throughout this domain, the density is positive for arbitrarily large momentum magnitudes. This is a fixed relative-shell effective Newtonian model, distinct from the microcanonical preparation and Gibbs-volume entropy convention in [[post-tgr-kepler-microcanonical-volume-preparation]].

Here $m_1,m_2,G,r_0,R,h_*$ and $\beta$ are fixed inputs; the reduced mass $\mu$, coupling product $A$, and Hamiltonian $h$ are the specified derived constructions. The partition function, density, temperature parameter and response are derived within this selected preparation.

Because canonical momenta are unbounded, this preparation does not have the whole-ensemble slow-motion bound imposed on the separate bounded-energy microcanonical branch. The postulate makes no claim that either distribution is dynamically reached or empirically observed.

post-tgr-kepler-microcanonical-volume-pr.physical_scope: Effective Newtonian relative two-body shell with r0>0 and R>16r0, energy A/R<e≤A/(16r0), explicit Gibbs-volume entropy convention, and optional stated uniform slow-motion restriction; no center-of-mass response or empirical thermalization claim.

post-tgr-kepler-microcanonical-volume-pr:
## Postulate

Adopt the relative Hamiltonian, shell $r_0\le|q|\le R$, parameters $\mu,A,r_0,R,h_*$, phase-volume function $\Omega(E)$, and shell measure from [[def-tgr-regulated-kepler-shell-law]]. For $E=-e$ in the branch
$$\frac AR<e\le\frac{A}{16r_0},\qquad \delta:=\frac{er_0}{A}\in(0,1/16],$$
adopt the normalized energy-shell probability $P_E=\Sigma_E/\Omega'(E)$, whose total mass and support on $h=E$ are established by [[lem-tgr-regulated-kepler-shell-law-normalization]]. Adopt the Gibbs-volume entropy convention $S_G(E)=k_B\log\Omega(E)$, define $1/T_G=dS_G/dE$ where this derivative is positive, and define $C_G=dE/dT_G$ where the derivative exists. These are the selected finite-system preparation and temperature conventions; they are not asserted to be universal operational identifications.

For a physical Newtonian slow-motion regime, additionally require a stated dimensionless tolerance $0<\delta_{\rm NR}\ll1$ and
$$\frac{2A}{\mu r_0c^2}\le\delta_{\rm NR}.$$
On the adopted negative-energy shell, $|p|/\mu$ then has the corresponding uniform speed bound. This condition restricts the microcanonical branch only; it is not imposed by or transferred to the distinct canonical preparation. No center-of-mass degree of freedom, dynamical wall law, empirical thermalization, or self-consistent relativistic field is included.

The masses, $G$, $r_0$, $R$, $h_*$, selected energy $E$, and any $\delta_{\rm NR}$ tolerance are fixed inputs. The reduced mass $\mu$, $A=Gm_1m_2$, relative Hamiltonian, phase-volume function, and entropy/temperature/response quantities are defined constructions of this model; none is asserted to be universal across gravitational frameworks.

pthm-tgr-regulated-ensemble-response-ine.physical_scope: Same fixed relative Kepler Hamiltonian and radial shell, with Gibbs-volume microcanonical versus canonical preparation. At E=−A/(32r0), R>32r0, and 2A/(μr0c²)≤δNR≪1, the microcanonical branch is slow-motion and has CG<0; the canonical model has CK≥0 but retains unbounded momentum tails. No equivalence or thermalization is asserted.

pthm-tgr-regulated-ensemble-response-ine:
## Statement

Use the same positive relative parameters $\mu,A,r_0,R,h_*$ and fixed Hamiltonian $h(q,p)=|p|^2/(2\mu)-A/|q|$ for both preparations in [[post-tgr-kepler-microcanonical-volume-preparation]] and [[post-tgr-kepler-canonical-preparation]]. Let $R>32r_0$, choose $E=-e=-A/(32r_0)$, and assume the microcanonical physical applicability condition
$$\frac{2A}{\mu r_0c^2}\le\delta_{\rm NR}\ll1.$$
Then the Gibbs-volume microcanonical response satisfies $C_G(E)<0$, while the separate canonical preparation has $C_K(\beta)\ge0$ for every $\beta>0$. For its density $p_\beta$, define $\langle g\rangle_\beta:=\int g p_\beta\,d\nu_{\rm rel}$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(h):=\int(h-\langle h\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\nu_{\rm rel}$. The microcanonical energy lies on the strictly negative-capacity branch and obeys the stated uniform slow-speed bound. The canonical model has unbounded momentum support, so this theorem makes no whole-ensemble slow-speed claim about it. The signs concern different finite-system preparations and do not contradict one another; neither sign establishes that nature realizes the model or that either preparation is dynamically attained.
lem-tgr-finite-static-mode-occupation-tr:
## Statement

Let $M\ge0$ be an integer, let $E_1,\ldots,E_M\in\mathbb R$, $\beta>0$, and $\mu\in\mathbb R$. Define the finite index set $\mathcal N_M=\{0,1\}^M$ and the finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H_M=\mathbb C^{\mathcal N_M}$ with orthonormal basis $|n_1,\ldots,n_M\rangle$. Define diagonal operators $H$ and $N$ on this basis by
$$H|\mathbf n\rangle=\left(\sum_{j=1}^M E_jn_j\right)|\mathbf n\rangle,\qquad N|\mathbf n\rangle=\left(\sum_{j=1}^M n_j\right)|\mathbf n\rangle.$$
For a matrix on $\mathcal H_M$, trace means the finite sum of its diagonal entries in this basis. Then
$$\Xi=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta(H-\mu N)}=\prod_{j=1}^M\left(1+e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu)}\right)\in(0,\infty).$$
The normalized diagonal state with weights $\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta(\sum_j E_jn_j-\mu\sum_jn_j)}$ has, for each $1\le j\le M$, occupation mean
$$\langle n_j\rangle=\frac{1}{e^{\beta(E_j-\mu)}+1}.$$
For $M=0$, the empty product and trace are $1$, and there are no occupation marginals. This is a finite-dimensional algebraic identity and uses no choice principle, curved-space spectrum, or gravitational field equation.

post-tgr-fixed-static-gas-preparation.physical_scope: Classical ideal gas on a prescribed smooth static finite region with lapse bounded strictly above zero, or a separately declared finite-mode exclusion regulator. The metric is fixed input, not an Einstein solution sourced by the gas; no generic curved-space quantum spectrum or observed equilibrium is asserted.

post-tgr-fixed-static-gas-preparation:
## Postulate

For the classical branch, prescribe a smooth static metric on a neighborhood of $I_{x^0}\times\overline B$, where $I_{x^0}\subset\mathbb R$ is an open interval and $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ is an open bounded coordinate box with compact closure and positive volume:
$$g=-\mathcal N(x)^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(x)dx^i dx^j,\qquad x^0=ct.$$
Here $h_{ij}$ is a smooth positive-definite spatial metric whose eigenvalues are bounded above and away from zero, and the dimensionless lapse satisfies $0<\mathcal N_0\le\mathcal N(x)\le\mathcal N_1<\infty$. The static chart and observer congruence are distinct objects: with $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$, the static unit observer is $u=\mathcal N^{-1}\xi$, satisfying $g(u,u)=-1$, under the conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. This geometry is prescribed and is not assumed to solve an Einstein equation with gas stress as source.

Take particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, $c>0$ in metres per second, orthonormal momentum $\hat p\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and adopt the massive-particle dispersion function $E(\hat p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p|^2}$ in joules as a model input. The Killing energy is the derived function $H_K(x,\hat p)=\mathcal N(x)E(\hat p)$, and the action reference $h_*>0$ is in joule-seconds. For the classical ideal-gas branch, take $M\ge1$ independent particles with no interparticle potential, the $1/M!$ phase-counting convention, inverse Killing-energy parameter $\beta_K>0$ in inverse joules, and dimensionless fugacity $z>0$. The finite proper-phase normalization is supplied by [[lem-tgr-static-gas-finite-normalization]]. There is no interaction term or gas-induced change of the metric in this branch.

As a distinct finite quantum regulator, one may instead specify a finite mode set $J=\{1,\ldots,M\}$, $M\ge0$, positive dimensionless lapse values $\mathcal N_j$, and momenta $\hat p_j\in\mathbb R^3$. Adopt mode energies $E_j=\mathcal N_j\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p_j|^2}$, canonical parameter $\beta_K>0$ in inverse joules, and chemical-potential parameter $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ in joules, together with the finite occupation basis $n_j\in\{0,1\}$. The associated finite trace and occupation identity are given by [[lem-tgr-finite-static-mode-occupation-trace]]. This is an explicitly supplied spectral cutoff, not a claim that arbitrary curved spacetime has these modes. Neither branch reports an observation or asserts actual thermalization.

The metric $h_{ij}$, lapse $\mathcal N$, region, $m,c,h_*$, canonical parameters and (in the finite-mode branch) the mode list are supplied inputs. The local energy, Killing-energy weight, partition functions, normalized state, local densities and response identities are derived constructions under the stated mathematical results; no universal equation of state or metric backreaction is assumed.

pthm-tgr-static-gas-local-equilibrium.physical_scope: Exact classical ideal-gas normalization, redshifted local thermodynamic parameters, pressure and hydrostatic identity on the prescribed bounded-lapse static background, plus the separate finite-mode trace identity. No Einstein backreaction, generic curved-space mode spectrum, self-gravitating star, or empirical equilibrium assertion.

pthm-tgr-static-gas-local-equilibrium:
## Statement

Assume the prescribed static background and either preparation branch in [[post-tgr-fixed-static-gas-preparation]]. In the classical branch, the one-particle Killing-energy partition integral is strictly positive and finite; for $M\ge1$ identical classical particles $Z_M=Z_1^M/M!$, and grand fugacity $z>0$ gives $\Xi=e^{zZ_1}$. With $f(x,\hat p)=zh_*^{-3}e^{-\beta_K\mathcal N(x)E(\hat p)}$, define proper local number density $n=\int f\,d^3\hat p$, energy density $\varepsilon=\int E f\,d^3\hat p$, and isotropic pressure $P=\frac13\int\hat p\cdot\nabla_{\hat p}E\,f\,d^3\hat p$. Then
$$T_{\rm loc}(x)=\frac{T_K}{\mathcal N(x)},\qquad P=nk_BT_{\rm loc},\qquad \partial_iP=-(\varepsilon+P)\partial_i\log\mathcal N,$$
where $T_K=(k_B\beta_K)^{-1}$. If $z=e^{\beta_K\mu_K}$, then $\mu_{\rm loc}=\mu_K/\mathcal N$.

In the finite fermion-mode branch, let $E_j=\mathcal N_j\epsilon_j$ with $\epsilon_j=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p_j|^2}$, $\mathcal N_j>0$, $\beta_K>0$, and $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$. The normalized diagonal state has
$$\langle n_j\rangle=\frac{1}{e^{\beta_K(E_j-\mu_K)}+1}=\frac{1}{e^{\beta_j(\epsilon_j-\mu_j)}+1},\qquad \beta_j=\beta_K\mathcal N_j,\quad \mu_j=\frac{\mu_K}{\mathcal N_j}.$$
Both conclusions are conditional model deductions on the fixed background or finite supplied mode set. They assert no Einstein equation, gas backreaction, arbitrary curved-space spectrum, or observed equilibrium.

ex-tgr-physical-finite-softened-box.physical_scope: One explicit finite box and positive softening instance of the adopted effective Newtonian preparation; establishes a normalized model probability, not observed equilibration or a claim about a real gravitating gas.

cex-tgr-physical-unregulated-collapse.physical_scope: Refutes finite-volume sufficiency for the exact unregulated two-point Newtonian canonical weight, for arbitrary positive masses. The collision limit is outside a controlled weak-field Newtonian regime and is not asserted to describe a real short-distance source.

ex-tgr-physical-negative-kepler-capacity.physical_scope: One energy and shell-radius instance of the finite regulated relative Kepler model under its declared Gibbs-volume convention and weak-field restriction; the canonical comparison remains a distinct preparation with unbounded momenta.

ex-tgr-physical-static-lapse-two.physical_scope: Classical ideal gas on a prescribed flat finite box with constant dimensionless lapse two and a stated Killing-generator normalization; the local temperature parameter is T_K/2 and is not a reported measurement.
